scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Regular trajectories, pruning and quantum parity” (preprints/Regular-trajectories-pruning-and-quantum-parity-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 274 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 de3f7a04ba137876), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix positive integers d, k, C and a real 0 < ε ≤ 1/2. There is an integer n0 = n0(d, k, C, ε) such that, for every n ≥ n0, every allowed circuit of depth at most d on at most C(n + 1)k total qubits has an input x ∈ {0, 1}n on which its answer equals PARITYn(x) with probability strictly less than 1/2 + ε.
